function.description:
Collect structured multiple-choice answers from the user. Use this tool only when you are blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one you cannot resolve from the request, the code, or sensible defaults.

Usage notes:
- Each question should have at least 2 options for the user to choose from
- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use allow_multiple: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Prefer this tool over listing options in your final response text (as letters, numbers, bullet points, etc).
function.name: AskQuestion

questions.description: Array of questions to present to the user (minimum 1 required)

allow_multiple.description: If true, user can select multiple options. Defaults to false.

prompt.description: The question text to display to the user

title.description: Optional title for the questions form

function.name: CallMcpTool

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the MCP tool, as described in the tool descriptor.

server.description: Identifier of the MCP server hosting the tool.

toolName.description: Name of the MCP tool to invoke.

function.description:
Deletes a file at the specified path. The operation will fail gracefully if:
    - The file doesn't exist
    - The operation is rejected for security reasons
    - The file cannot be deleted
function.name: Delete

path.description: The absolute path of the file to delete

function.description: Reads a specific resource from an MCP server, identified by server name and resource URI. Optionally, set downloadPath (relative to the workspace) to save the resource to disk; when set, the resource will be downloaded and not returned to the model.
function.name: FetchMcpResource

downloadPath.description: Optional relative path in the workspace to save the resource to. When set, the resource is written to disk and is not returned to the model.

function.description:
Tool to search for files matching a glob pattern

- Works fast with codebases of any size
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time
- Primary tool for exploring directory trees: use target_directory and glob_pattern (e.g. "**/*") to inspect the full recursive file tree or understand the deep nested structure of a directory or module in a single call.
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns, extensions, or directory hierarchies.
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively perform multiple searches that are potentially useful as a batch.
function.name: Glob

glob_pattern.description:
The glob pattern to match files against.
Patterns not starting with "**/" are automatically prepended with "**/" to enable recursive searching.

Examples:
	- "*.js" (becomes "**/*.js") - find all .js files
	- "**/node_modules/**" - find all node_modules directories
	- "**/test/**/test_*.ts" - find all test_*.ts files in any test directory

target_directory.description: Absolute path to directory to search for files in. If not provided, defaults to Cursor workspace root.

function.description: A search tool built on ripgrep. Results are capped to several thousand output lines for responsiveness; when truncation occurs, the results report "at least" counts, but are otherwise accurate.
function.name: Grep

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-i.description: Case insensitive search (rg -i) Defaults to false

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

head_limit.description: Limit output size. For "content" mode: limits total matches shown. For "files_with_matches" and "count" modes: limits number of files.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

offset.description: Skip first N entries. For "content" mode: skips first N matches. For "files_with_matches" and "count" modes: skips first N files. Use with head_limit for pagination.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "content".

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg pattern -- PATH). Defaults to Cursor workspace root.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

function.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- You can optionally specify a line offset and limit (especially handy for long files), but it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters
- Lines in the output are numbered starting at 1, using following format: LINE_NUMBER|LINE_CONTENT
- You have the capability to call multiple tools in a single response. It is always better to speculatively read multiple files as a batch that are potentially useful.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive 'File is empty.'

Image Support:
- This tool can also read image files when called with the appropriate path.
- Supported image formats: jpeg/jpg, png, gif, webp.

PDF Support:
- PDF files are converted into text content automatically (subject to the same character limits as other files).
function.name: Read

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Positive values are 1-indexed from the start of the file. Negative values count backwards from the end (e.g. -1 is the last line). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

function.description:
Lists files and directories under a directory path.

Use this tool only when you need immediate children (1 level) of a directory without recursion.
When you need to view the full recursive file tree or understand the deep nested structure of a directory or module, prefer Glob with a recursive pattern (e.g. target_directory: "path/to/dir", glob_pattern: "**/*") instead of issuing repetitive Ls calls on every subfolder.

You may provide ignore globs for large or irrelevant directories such as .git, node_modules, dist, build, .cursor-local-assistant-v2/history, or logs.
function.name: Ls

ignore.description: Optional ignore globs for directories or files that should be skipped while listing.

path.description: The absolute path of the directory to list.

function.description: Read and display linter errors from the current workspace. You can provide paths to specific files or directories, or omit the argument to get diagnostics for all files.
function.name: ReadLints

paths.description: Optional. An array of paths to files or directories to read linter errors for. You can use either relative paths in the workspace or absolute paths. If provided, returns diagnostics for the specified files/directories only. If not provided, returns diagnostics for all files in the workspace.

function.description:
Executes a given command in a shell session, waiting for output for `block_until_ms` millis.
You can monitor commands by configuring `notify_on_output`. You will be notified at the end of your turn whenever stdout/stderr output matches the regex `pattern`. Output redirected only to a file will not trigger it. Configure a 5-or-fewer-word `reason` explaining what you are watching for, and optionally configure `debounce_ms`.
function.name: Shell

block_until_ms.description: How long to block and wait for the command to complete before moving it to background (in milliseconds). Defaults to 30000ms (30 seconds). Set to 0 to immediately run the command in the background. The timer includes the shell startup time.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words

working_directory.description: The absolute path to the working directory to execute the command in (defaults to current directory)

notify_on_output.description: Optional watcher for backgrounded command output. You will be notified at the end of your turn whenever output matches the regex pattern. Use stable sentinel lines and simple anchored regexes; do not match all output. Completion notifications are separate and do not require this field.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against command output.

reason.description: Five or fewer words describing what you are watching for. The UI prefixes it as Monitored `reason`.

debounce_ms.description: Minimum milliseconds between notifications. Values below 5000ms are treated as 5000ms.

notification_limit.description: Optional maximum number of output-match notifications for this command.

function.name: AwaitShell
function.description:
Check or poll a backgrounded Shell job. Use this after Shell returns a shell_id. If Shell returned a shell_id for a known background job, every AwaitShell call for that job MUST pass that exact non-empty shell_id. Never omit shell_id or pass an empty string when polling a known background job. Omitting shell_id is allowed only when there is no known background job and the caller intentionally wants a timed wait. If multiple jobs are running, explicitly pass the shell_id for the intended job. Pattern matching checks accumulated stdout/stderr content, not terminal metadata.

Do not poll reflexively while unrelated work can continue. However, you MUST call AwaitShell with the matching shell_id before reporting that a background job has completed, passed, failed, produced an artifact, or is ready for the user. This is required whenever the user's request depends on the job result, including builds, tests, deployments, downloads, migrations, packaging, and artifact generation.

If ending the turn while a job is still running, explicitly state that it is still running; do not imply completion. Do not mark a related task complete or send a final result until AwaitShell returns completion for that job. After AwaitShell reports completion, inspect the exit code and final output. For commands expected to generate files, also verify the expected artifact exists before reporting its path.

shell_id.description: Optional shell id to poll. Required when block_until_ms is 0.

block_until_ms.description: Max time to wait before returning, in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000ms. Set to 0 for a non-blocking status check.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against accumulated stdout/stderr content. Uses multiline matching.

function.description: Writes literal characters to an existing background shell session. Use only when a previous Shell result returned a shell_id and the process is waiting for stdin. Include any needed newline in chars.
function.name: WriteShellStdin

chars.description: Literal characters to write to stdin. Include \n when submitting a line.

shell_id.description: The shell_id returned by a backgrounded Shell command.

function.description: Requests that a running Shell tool call move to the background so the current agent turn can continue. Pass the original Shell tool_call_id, not the shell_id.
function.name: ForceBackgroundShell

tool_call_id.description: The original Shell tool call id to move to background.

function.name: PatchEdit
function.description:
Edit an existing text file by replacing exact text copied from the latest Read. Use this as the default tool for modifying existing source, markdown, JSON, YAML, config files, and short inline spans.

Usage:
- Read the relevant file first, then copy the exact current text into old_string.
- path must be an absolute file path. Do not pass a relative path, workspace-relative path, or bare filename; this tool will not resolve or rewrite it.
- old_string must exactly match the current file content; line endings are not normalized or treated equivalently during matching.
- By default replace_all is false and old_string must match exactly one occurrence. If it matches multiple occurrences, the tool reports an error.
- Set replace_all to true only when every exact occurrence should be replaced.
- new_string may be empty to delete old_string.
- Write is still only for creating new files or intentionally rewriting a whole file.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify. Required forms include /abs/path on macOS/Linux, C:\abs\path or C:/abs/path on Windows, or //server/share/path for UNC paths. Relative paths are invalid.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current file content exactly and must not be empty.

new_string.description: Replacement text. May be empty to delete old_string.

replace_all.description: Whether to replace all exact occurrences. Defaults to false.

function.description:
Switch the interaction mode to better match the current task. Each mode is optimized for a specific type of work.

## When to Switch Modes

Switch modes proactively when:
1. **Task type changes** - User shifts from asking questions to requesting implementation, or vice versa
2. **Complexity emerges** - What seemed simple reveals architectural decisions or multiple approaches
3. **Debugging needed** - An error, bug, or unexpected behavior requires investigation
4. **Planning needed** - The task is large, ambiguous, or has significant trade-offs to discuss
5. **You're stuck** - Multiple attempts without progress suggest a different approach is needed

## When NOT to Switch

Do NOT switch modes for:
- Simple, clear tasks that can be completed quickly in current mode
- Mid-implementation when you're making good progress
- Minor clarifying questions (just ask them)
- Tasks where the current mode is working well

## Available Modes

### Agent Mode [switchable]
Default implementation mode with full access to all tools for making changes.

**Switch to Agent when:**
- You have a clear understanding of what to implement
- Planning/debugging is complete and you're ready to code
- The task is straightforward with an obvious implementation
- You've gathered enough context and are ready to execute

**Examples:**
- After planning: "I've designed the approach, ready to implement" -> Switch to Agent
- After debugging: "Found the bug, it's a null check issue" -> Switch to Agent
- Simple task: User asks to "Add a comment to this function" -> Stay in Agent (no switch needed)

### Plan Mode [switchable]
Investigation-first collaborative mode for designing implementation approaches. It may create a minimal workspace planning artifact only when the user explicitly requests one.

**Switch to Plan when:**
- The task has multiple valid approaches with significant trade-offs
- Architectural decisions are needed (e.g., "Add caching" - Redis vs in-memory vs file-based)
- The task touches many files or systems (large refactors, migrations)
- Requirements are unclear and you need to explore before understanding scope
- You would otherwise ask multiple clarifying questions

**Examples:**
- User: "Add user authentication" -> Switch to Plan (session vs JWT, storage, middleware decisions)
- User: "Refactor the database layer" -> Switch to Plan (large scope, architectural impact)
- User: "Make the app faster" -> Switch to Plan (need to profile, multiple optimization strategies)

### Debug Mode (cannot switch to this mode)
Systematic troubleshooting mode for investigating bugs, failures, and unexpected behavior with runtime evidence.

### Ask Mode (cannot switch to this mode)
Read-only mode for exploring code and answering questions without making changes.

## Important Notes

- **Be proactive**: Don't wait for the user to ask you to switch modes
- **Explain briefly**: When switching, briefly explain why in your `explanation` parameter
- **Don't over-switch**: If the current mode is working, stay in it
- **User approval required**: Mode switches require user consent
function.name: SwitchMode

explanation.description: Optional explanation for why the mode switch is requested. This helps the user understand why you're switching modes.

target_mode_id.description: The mode to switch to. Allowed values: 'plan', 'agent'.

function.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Task tool launches specialized subagents (subprocesses) that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each subagent_type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

SUBAGENT & DELEGATION POLICY:
Proactively leverage Subagents whenever offloading work provides a concrete benefit in speed, context isolation, or parallelism over running everything in the foreground.

When to use Task:
- Broad Codebase Exploration & Scans: Use subagent_type="explore" or "generalPurpose" to search codebase architecture, find API endpoints, trace dependencies, or inspect large sets of files without polluting the main context window.
- Parallel Execution: When a feature or refactoring naturally splits into decoupled parts (e.g. Frontend vs Backend, multiple modules, unit test creation alongside implementation), launch concurrent subagents in a single batch.
- Bounded Implementation / Fixes: Dispatch self-contained subtasks (creating new components, writing tests, isolated bug fixes) with clear interface boundaries.
- Heavy Noise & Log Isolation: Isolate long test traces, terminal outputs, build logs, or extensive diff reviews.

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- Simple, single-file lookups or 1-2 quick edits that can be done immediately.
- Purely conversational answers.

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do.
- Provide a clear, structured prompt covering Objective, Scope, Constraints, Expected Output, and Done Criteria.
- The subagent's outputs should generally be trusted; synthesize concise summaries for the user.
- Agents can be resumed using the `resume` parameter to reuse existing context.

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or answer questions about the codebase.
- shell: Command execution specialist for running bash commands, git operations, and terminal tasks.
- browser-use: Perform browser-based testing and web automation.
- Custom subagents: Use the exact `name` of a matching agent listed in the `<subagents>` context (for example `advisor`, `planner`, `debugger`, or `tester`). Choose custom subagents when their specialized role matches the task. Built-in types remain appropriate when no listed custom agent is a better fit.

Available models:
- fast: Extremely fast, cost-effective model for quick searches and tightly scoped changes.
- Default model (unspecified): Inherits parent model for complex multi-step reasoning or high-quality code generation.
function.name: Task

attachments.description: Optional array of file paths to videos to pass to video-review subagents. Files are read and attached to the subagent's context. Supports video formats (mp4, webm) for Gemini models.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

model.description: Optional model to use for this agent. If not specified, inherits from parent. Prefer fast for quick, straightforward tasks to minimize cost and latency. Only select a different model when the task specifically benefits from it (e.g., deep reasoning, high-quality code review, multimodal input)

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

readonly.description: If true, the subagent will run in readonly mode ("Ask mode") with restricted write operations and no MCP access.

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, sends a follow-up message to the agent when its turn is complete.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type to use for this task. Use a built-in type such as generalPurpose, explore, shell, or browser-use; or use the exact `name` of a matching agent listed in the `<subagents>` context.

function.description: Use this tool to create and manage a structured task list for your current coding session.
function.name: TodoWrite

merge.description: Whether to merge the todos with the existing todos. If true, the todos will be merged into the existing todos based on the id field. Use true for normal incremental updates, marking items complete, adding follow-ups, or changing the current in-progress item. If false, the new todos replace the entire list and must include every existing todo id once a list already exists.

todos.description: Array of TODO items to update or create

content.description: The description/content of the todo item. For merge=true updates, omit content when it is unchanged. New todos and merge=false replacements must include content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TODO item

status.description: The current status of the TODO item. For merge=true updates, omit status when it is unchanged.

function.description: Fetch content from a specified URL and return its contents in a readable markdown format. Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content.
function.name: WebFetch

url.description: The URL to fetch. The content will be converted to a readable markdown format.

function.description: Search web for real-time info on any topic; use for up-to-date facts not in training data, like current events or tech updates. Results include snippets and URLs.
function.name: WebSearch

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this tool is being used, and how it contributes to the goal.

search_term.description: The search term to look up on the web. Be specific and include relevant keywords for better results. For technical queries, include version numbers or dates if relevant.

function.description:
Use this tool to create or revise a concise plan for accomplishing the user's request. It is available when saving or updating a plan in the plan UI would help the user. Use it only when the user requests a persisted plan or when an explicit planning workflow requires it; a textual plan is sufficient otherwise.

The plan you create should be properly formatted in markdown, using appropriate sections and headers. The plan should be very concise and actionable, providing the minimum amount of detail for the user to understand and action the plan. Cite specific file paths and essential snippets of code. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use markdown tables in plan content (they cannot be rendered for the user); use bullet lists instead. The first line MUST BE A TITLE for the plan formatted as a level 1 markdown heading.

TASK ORGANIZATION:

Use 'todos' for organizing implementation tasks:
- Each todo should be a clear, specific, and actionable task
- Each todo needs a unique ID (e.g., "setup-auth") and descriptive content
- If the plan is simple, provide just a few high-level todos or none at all

UPDATING THE PLAN:
- If a current plan already exists, submit the complete revised plan and omit the name field
- Only the first CreatePlan call may include name; later calls must not include name and must not use name to rename or create a separate plan

Additional guidelines:
- Avoid asking clarifying questions in the plan itself. Ask them before calling this tool using the AskQuestion tool.
- Todos help break down complex plans into manageable, trackable tasks
- Focus on high-level meaningful decisions rather than low-level implementation details
- A good plan is glanceable, not a wall of text.
function.name: CreatePlan

name.description: A short 3-4 word name for the plan. IMPORTANT: Provide this only on the first CreatePlan call when no current plan exists. If a current plan already exists, omit this field entirely; do not use it to rename or create a separate plan.

overview.description: A 1-2 sentence high-level description of the plan that summarizes what will be accomplished

plan.description: A detailed, concrete plan for accomplishing the user's request

function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- path must be an absolute file path. Do not pass a relative path, workspace-relative path, or bare filename; this tool will not resolve or rewrite it.
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the User.
function.name: Write

contents.description: The contents to write to the file

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify. Required forms include /abs/path on macOS/Linux, C:\abs\path or C:/abs/path on Windows, or //server/share/path for UNC paths. Relative paths are invalid.

function.description:
Generate an image file from a text description.

STRICT INVOCATION RULES (must follow):
- Only use this tool when the user explicitly asks for an image. Do not generate images "just to be helpful".
- Do not use this tool for data heavy visualizations such as charts, plots, tables.

General guidelines:
- Provide a concrete description first: subject(s), layout, style, colors, text (if any), and constraints.
- If the user requests an aspect ratio, set `aspect_ratio` to one of "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "16:9", or "9:16".
- If the user provides reference images, include them in `reference_image_paths`.
- Do not repeat generated images as Markdown in your response; the client displays tool-generated images automatically.

Examples that should call this tool:
- user: "Generate an app icon for a note-taking app, minimal flat vector style." (explicitly requests an image asset)
- user: "Make a UI mockup of a settings screen with a dark mode toggle." (explicitly requests a UI mockup)
- user: "Generate an asset of a game character with a sword." (explicitly requests a visual asset)

Examples that should not call this tool:
- user: "Create a plan to refactor this module." (planning request; respond in text or mermaid diagram)
- user: "Generate a chart of sales and revenue using data.csv." (data visualization; generate via code)
function.name: GenerateImage

aspect_ratio.description: Optional aspect ratio for the generated image. Supported values are "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "16:9", and "9:16".

description.description: A detailed description of the image to generate.

filename.description: Optional filename for the generated image (e.g., 'diagram.png'). Do not include a directory path - the tool automatically handles where to save and how to display the image. If not provided, a timestamped filename will be generated.

image_data.description: Optional raw base64 image data if the model directly produced image bytes. Do not include data:image/...;base64, prefix.

reference_image_paths.description: Optional array of file paths to reference images as additional inputs.

function.name: SembleSearch
function.description:
Semantic code search for focused technical investigation. Prefer fast-context MCP first when it is available for broad codebase discovery, architecture/behavior exploration, or tracing feature flows. Use SembleSearch to narrow an investigation to specific symbols, algorithms, or implementation details, or when fast-context MCP is unavailable. The repo parameter must be the absolute workspace directory.

Write queries in natural English; keep identifiers and code fragments intact. For exact text/regex matches, use Grep. To expand a SembleSearch result and trace connected code, use SembleFindRelated.

description.description: Short plain-language description of what this search will find. One sentence; do not include tool names or argument keys.

repo.description: Absolute local repository directory or explicit HTTP(S) Git URL.

query.description: Focused English behavior description, exact symbol name, literal, or code fragment.

content.description: Content scope. Use all sparingly because it broadens and weakens ranking.

top_k.description: Number of ranked chunks to return.

max_snippet_lines.description: Maximum source lines returned per result. Use 0 for locations only.

function.name: SembleFindRelated
function.description: Find code semantically related to a known SembleSearch result. Use immediately after SembleSearch to expand context, trace callers, collaborators, or connected implementations. Pass the exact file_path and line number from the search result.

description.description: Short plain-language description of the relationship being explored. One sentence; do not include tool names or argument keys.

repo.description: The same absolute local repository directory or explicit HTTP(S) Git URL used for search.

file_path.description: File path exactly as returned by SembleSearch.

line.description: One-indexed line contained by the source result.

content.description: Content scope containing the source file.

top_k.description: Number of ranked related chunks to return.

max_snippet_lines.description: Maximum source lines returned per result. Use 0 for locations only.

function.name: EditNotebook
function.description:
Use this tool to edit a jupyter notebook cell.
Cell indices are 0-based. 'old_string' and 'new_string' should be a valid cell content, i.e. WITHOUT any JSON syntax that notebook files use under the hood. If you need to create a new notebook, just set 'is_new_cell' to true and cell_idx to 0.

cell_idx.description: The index of the cell to edit (0-based)

cell_language.description: The language of the cell to edit. Should be STRICTLY one of these: 'python', 'markdown', 'javascript', 'typescript', 'r', 'sql', 'shell', 'raw' or 'other'.

is_new_cell.description: If true, a new cell will be created at the specified cell index. If false, the cell at the specified cell index will be edited.

new_string.description: The edited text to replace the old_string or the content for the new cell.

old_string.description: The text to replace (must be unique within the cell, and must match the cell contents exactly, including all whitespace and indentation).

target_notebook.description: The path to the notebook file you want to edit. You can use either a relative path in the workspace or an absolute path. If an absolute path is provided, it will be preserved as is.

function.name: GetMcpTools
function.description:
Inspect the Cursor client's current MCP server state. Use this only when a server or tool is absent from <mcp_meta_tools>, when its descriptor has neither an inline schema nor a readable definition_path, or when you specifically need refreshed connection/authentication status. Do not call it before tools already described in <mcp_meta_tools>.

1. {"server":"<id>"}: returns the server status, instructions, descriptions, and schemas.
2. {"server":"<id>","toolName":"<name>"}: returns one tool.
3. {"pattern":"<regex>"}: searches server and tool names.
4. {"server":"<id>","pattern":"<regex>"}: searches one server.
5. No arguments: returns the full catalog; use only as a last resort.

If an MCP call reports an authentication error, call that server's mcp_auth tool with empty arguments when available, then retry the original call only if authentication succeeds.

pattern.description: RE2 regex pattern to search server and tool names (max 256 chars). Optionally combine with server to scope the search.

toolName.description: Tool name within the server. Requires server to be set.

function.name: InspectChanges
function.description:
Inspects uncommitted Git changes (status and diff) for a workspace repository or specific files with structured, token-safe summaries.

Use this tool for:
- Inspecting uncommitted changes or diff across the workspace or for a batch of files in one call (`files: ["src/main.rs", "Cargo.toml"]`).
- Checking change manifest only without diff overhead (`mode: "summary"`).
- Isolating staged index changes (`scope: "staged"`) or unstaged changes (`scope: "unstaged"`).
- Reviewing repository-wide diffs without flooding context with raw terminal output (`mode: "review"` or `mode: "diff"`).

Usage Guidelines:
- Pass the absolute project/repo directory path (e.g. `path: "C:/path/to/repo"`).
- Use `mode: "summary"` when only an inventory of changed files is needed before selecting specific diffs.
- Use `files` with repository-relative paths to retrieve diffs for multiple specific files in a single tool call.
- Use `scope: "staged"` or `scope: "unstaged"` to filter index vs working tree changes.
- Automatically filters large binary files and lockfiles to preserve token budget.

path.description: The absolute path to the Git repository directory or a specific file to inspect.

mode.description: Output mode: summary returns manifest only; diff returns selected diffs; review returns manifest and bounded diff.

scope.description: Git change scope: all, staged index changes, or unstaged working-tree changes.

files.description: Optional repository-relative exact paths to inspect in one call.

max_files.description: Maximum manifest files returned. Values above the server limit are clamped.

max_diff_chars.description: Maximum combined diff characters returned. Values above the server limit are clamped.

function.name: GitArchaeology
function.description:
Investigates Git repository history to understand why code exists, when a behavior changed, and find originating commits.

Use this tool instead of running `git log`, `git blame`, or `git show` via Shell:
- `lineage`: Trace the source commits of specific lines in a file (tracks moves across files and ignores whitespace changes).
- `pickaxe`: Find commits that added or removed a specific symbol, keyword, or regex pattern across the codebase.
- `file_biography`: Inspect a file's creation commit, rename history, and major change timeline.
- `commit_context`: Inspect detailed commit metadata, author, full message, and diffstat for a specific revision.

Usage Guidelines:
- Always provide absolute path for `repository`.
- Use `lineage` when investigating why a code block exists or who introduced it.
- Use `pickaxe` when searching for when a function, config, or bug pattern was introduced/deleted.
- Treat commit messages as historical evidence, not proof of undocumented intent.

repository.description: Absolute path to the Git repository or a path inside it.

path.description: Repository-relative path. Required for `lineage` and `file_biography`; optional filter for `pickaxe`.

end_line.description: Last source line for `lineage` (inclusive). Defaults to `start_line`.

regex.description: Use Git `-G` regex diff search instead of literal `-S` occurrence-change search.

limit.description: Maximum history records to return, 1 through 30. Defaults to 20.

commit.description: Commit hash or Git revision for `commit_context`.

function.name: Outline
function.description:
Extracts the high-level outline and symbol structure of a source file (classes, interfaces, structs, enums, methods, functions, fields, signatures, visibility, line ranges) using in-process Tree-sitter AST parsing.

Supported Languages:
Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Rust, Go, C, C++, C#, Dart.

When to use Outline:
- Inspecting large or unfamiliar files (>200 lines) to get a complete architectural map and API contract without reading the entire body.
- Locating exact method or class line ranges before making surgical edits with `Read` (using `offset`/`limit`) or `StrReplace`.
- Checking class hierarchy, implemented interfaces, fields, and method signatures.
- Conserving token budget and avoiding context window bloat.

When NOT to use Outline:
- Reading the implementation logic/body of a specific function (use `Read` with targeted `offset` and `limit` after locating it via `Outline`).
- Finding symbols across the entire repository (use `Grep` first).

Usage Guidelines:
- Always pass absolute file path (`path`).
- Language is automatically detected from file extension; `language` parameter is optional.

language.description: Optional explicit language identifier (e.g. 'java', 'rust', 'typescript', 'python', 'go', 'cpp', 'dart'). If omitted, language is detected from file extension.

path.description: The absolute path of the source file to inspect.

function.name: SymbolSearch
function.description: Finds code declarations structurally across one file or directory using in-process Tree-sitter parsing. Returns matching classes, interfaces, structs, enums, functions, methods, and types with file paths and line ranges. This performs syntax-based declaration search; it does not resolve language-server types, imports, or references.

exact_match.description: Require the symbol name to equal query exactly. Defaults to false.

kinds.description: Optional symbol-kind filters. Omit to search every supported kind.

max_results.description: Maximum matching declarations to return. Defaults to 50.

path.description: Absolute source file or directory to search.

query.description: Symbol name or name fragment to find.

function.name: StrReplace
function.description: Performs exact string replacements in files.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

function.name: UpdateCurrentStep
function.description: Record a concise (6 words or less), user-friendly update of the major step or phase you are working on for the parent timeline. Update when the subtask changes. Set `final_summary` and `completed_subtitle` ONCE per response as your last action before the final response. ALWAYS use in parallel with at least one other tool. ALWAYS start the update with a descriptive verb.

completed_subtitle.description: 4-6 word, past-tense, final summary of the work you have completed. Will be used as your agent subtitle in the UI. Keep the text concise, high-level, and user-friendly. Set this field ONCE per turn, as the last thing you do before your final response, at the same time that you set the final_summary field.

current_step.description: Major step or phase you are on. Update when the subtask changes. Keep the text concise, high-level, and user-friendly.

final_summary.description: User-facing executive summary succinctly reporting on your work / responding to the user's message; write this as a concise message speaking back to the user, not as a status tag. Typically 1-3 sentences, or a brief lead-in plus bullet points when there are multiple distinct takeaways, decisions, test results, etc. When using bullets, make them pleasant and easy to scan: 2-5 bullets when possible, one useful idea per bullet, ordered by importance to the user, concise but not cryptic, and no nested bullets unless the user requested detail. Use prose instead of bullets when there is only one main takeaway. Include the most relevant takeaways for the user, as implied by the user's original request. No unnecessary details. When answering questions by the user, include the full answer that the user is seeking. Examples of what to include: full answer(s) to user's question(s), high-level root cause while debugging, status update of completed (or in-progress) work, test results for specifically requested testing, blocking questions the user must answer before you can continue, links to newly created PRs, etc. Examples of what NOT to include (unless implicitly or explicitly requested by the user): tool calls / results, code / log / shell command excerpts, long file paths, line numbers, low-level implementation details, etc. Set this field just ONCE per turn, as the last thing you do before your final response, at the same time that you set the completed_subtitle field.

function.description:
Use this tool to create or revise a concise plan for accomplishing the user's request. This tool should be called at the end of the planning phase to finalize and store the plan.

The plan you create should be properly formatted in markdown, using appropriate sections and headers. The plan should be very concise and actionable, providing the minimum amount of detail for the user to understand and action the plan. It may be helpful to identify the most important couple files you will change, and existing code you will leverage. Cite specific file paths and essential snippets of code. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use markdown tables in plan content (they cannot be rendered for the user); use bullet lists instead. The first line MUST BE A TITLE for the plan formatted as a level 1 markdown heading.

TASK ORGANIZATION:

Use 'todos' for organizing implementation tasks:
- Each todo should be a clear, specific, and actionable task
- Each todo needs a unique ID (e.g., "setup-auth") and descriptive content
- If the plan is simple, provide just a few high-level todos or none at all

UPDATING THE PLAN:
- The plan file URI will be returned in the tool result
- If a current plan already exists, call this tool with the complete revised plan and omit the name field
- Only the first CreatePlan call may include name; later calls must not include name and must not use name to rename or create a separate plan
- If the user asks for a separate new plan while a current plan exists, explain the limitation or ask how to proceed before calling CreatePlan again

Additional guidelines:
- Avoid asking clarifying questions in the plan itself. Ask them before calling this tool. Present these to the user using the AskQuestion tool.
- Todos help break down complex plans into manageable, trackable tasks
- Focus on high-level meaningful decisions rather than low-level implementation details
- A good plan is glanceable, not a wall of text.
function.name: CreatePlan

name.description: A short 3-4 word name for the plan. IMPORTANT: Provide this only on the first CreatePlan call when no current plan exists. If a current plan already exists, omit this field entirely; do not use it to rename or create a separate plan.

overview.description: A 1-2 sentence high-level description of the plan that summarizes what will be accomplished

plan.description: A detailed, concrete plan for accomplishing the user's request

function.description: Deletes a file at the specified path. Use in plan mode only when the user explicitly requests removal of a planning artifact.
function.name: Delete

path.description: The absolute path of the file to delete

function.name: PatchEdit
function.description:
Edit an existing text file by replacing exact text copied from the latest Read. In plan mode, use only for an explicitly requested workspace planning artifact.

Usage:
- Read the relevant file first, then copy the exact current text into old_string.
- path must be an absolute file path. Do not pass a relative path, workspace-relative path, or bare filename.
- old_string must exactly match the current file content.
- replace_all defaults to false; set it to true only when every occurrence should change.
- new_string may be empty to delete the matched text.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify.

replace_all.description: Whether every exact occurrence should be replaced.

function.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.

The Task tool launches specialized subagents (subprocesses) that autonomously handle complex tasks. Each subagent_type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

SUBAGENT & DELEGATION POLICY:
Proactively leverage Subagents whenever offloading work provides a concrete benefit in speed, context isolation, or parallelism over running everything in the foreground.

When to use Task:
- Broad Codebase Exploration & Scans: Use subagent_type="explore" or "generalPurpose" to search codebase architecture, find API endpoints, trace dependencies, or inspect large sets of files without polluting the main context window.
- Parallel Execution: When an investigation or plan splits into decoupled domains (e.g. Protocol vs State model vs UI), launch concurrent subagents in a single batch.
- Bounded Implementation / Fixes: Dispatch self-contained subtasks with clear interface boundaries.
- Heavy Noise & Log Isolation: Isolate long test traces, terminal outputs, build logs, or extensive diff reviews.

When NOT to use the Task tool:
- Simple, single-file lookups or 1-2 quick edits that can be done immediately.
- Purely conversational answers.

Usage notes:
- Always include a short description (3-5 words) summarizing what the agent will do.
- Provide a clear, structured prompt covering Objective, Scope, Constraints, Expected Output, and Done Criteria.
- The subagent's outputs should generally be trusted; synthesize concise summaries for the user.
- Agents can be resumed using the `resume` parameter to reuse existing context.

Available subagent_types and a quick description of what they do:
- generalPurpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks.
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns, search code for keywords, or answer questions about the codebase.
- shell: Command execution specialist for running bash commands, git operations, and terminal tasks.
- browser-use: Perform browser-based testing and web automation.
- Custom subagents: Use the exact `name` of a matching agent listed in the `<subagents>` context (for example `advisor`, `planner`, `debugger`, or `tester`). Choose custom subagents when their specialized role matches the task. Built-in types remain appropriate when no listed custom agent is a better fit.

Available models:
- fast: Extremely fast, cost-effective model for quick searches and tightly scoped changes.
- Default model (unspecified): Inherits parent model for complex multi-step reasoning or high-quality code generation.
function.name: Task

attachments.description: Optional array of file paths to videos to pass to video-review subagents. Files are read and attached to the subagent's context. Supports video formats (mp4, webm) for Gemini models.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

model.description: Optional model to use for this agent. If not specified, inherits from parent. Prefer fast for quick, straightforward tasks to minimize cost and latency. Only select a different model when the task specifically benefits from it (e.g., deep reasoning, high-quality code review, multimodal input)

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

readonly.description: If true, the subagent will run in readonly mode ("Ask mode") with restricted write operations and no MCP access.

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, sends a follow-up message to the agent when its turn is complete.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type to use for this task. Use a built-in type such as generalPurpose, explore, shell, or browser-use; or use the exact `name` of a matching agent listed in the `<subagents>` context.

function.description: Writes a file to the local filesystem. In plan mode, use only when the user explicitly requests a workspace planning artifact; do not proactively create documentation or plan files.
function.name: Write

contents.description: The contents to write to the file

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify.

Use only when a previous Shell result returned a shell_id and the process is waiting for stdin. Include any needed newline in chars.
